# subject: # The interval algebra the three range kinds share, asserted underneath them:
# this package has no kind, no vocabulary and no sentence to read, so a row is
# an instant and the boundary it snaps to rather than an input and a rendering.
# Every instant is a literal and every zone is named. Nothing here reads the
# host clock or the host time zone, so the answers are the same numbers on
# `weekStart` is `-` for the default, 1, and 7 where the row exists to show the
# two disagree. Ends are exclusive throughout — `end of week` is the instant the
# next week begins, per design §3.1 — which is why an end never equals the last
# The Santiago rows are the reason `snap.ts` snaps after walking rather than
# before: 2026-09-06 has no local midnight there, and the day begins at 01:00.
# `window` rows are the `WINDOWS` table, written `start/end` with the wrap flag.
# Data, not code — a "night" that starts at 21:00 is a configuration change —
# and pinned here so that changing it is a decision rather than an accident.
